key_insight: JoHan shows that hand motion can be recovered more reliably by generating 2D and 3D hand poses jointly from video, instead of depending on noisy frame-by-frame pose estimates. This leads to more temporally consistent and occlusion-robust hand motion recovery.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing faithful 3D hand motion from video when hands are frequently occluded or only partially visible, which makes per-frame pose prediction unreliable and unstable over time.
method: A unified generative framework that takes video sequences as input and directly recovers hand motion end-to-end.
Jointly generates aligned 2D and 3D local hand pose sequences rather than using intermediate per-frame pose predictions.
Learns temporal consistency across frames to better handle occlusions and incomplete observations.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it can improve robustness in real-world video understanding tasks where hands are often blocked or motion is ambiguous. The approach also suggests a cleaner generative alternative to traditional pipeline-based pose estimation.

paper_title: Video-Conditioned Generative Joint 2D-3D Hand Motion Recovery
paper_authors: Chen Xu, Yunqi Li, Binbin Huang, Brent Yi, Shenghua Gao
